candidates.name: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome
support_spans: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
Eight lesions underwent biopsy, showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
candidates.why: The combination of skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and a specific genetic mutation in the SUFU gene supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Gorlin Syndrome
support_spans: Medical history was significant for a meningioma
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
candidates.why: The combination of skin lesions, a history of meningioma, and a mutation in the SUFU gene suggests Gorlin Syndrome.

selector.rationale: The presence of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules and a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, along with histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells, strongly supports Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome.

rejected.label: Gorlin Syndrome
rejected.why: While Gorlin Syndrome is related to Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome and shares the SUFU gene mutation, the specific combination of clinical and histopathological findings, including the type and location of papules, more closely aligns with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome.
